questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are horizontal unit vectors due east and due north respectively.]

Three forces, $(p\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})$ N, $(3\mathbf{i}-q\mathbf{j})$ N and $(q\mathbf{i}+2p\mathbf{j})$ N, where $p$ and $q$ are constants, act on a particle of mass 2 kg. The forces cause the particle to move with acceleration $(\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the direction of the acceleration, giving your answer as a bearing to the nearest degree.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\tan\theta = \frac{3}{1}$
A1: $\theta = 71.565°...$
A1: Bearing is $162°$ (nearest degree)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (Whole question) Accept use of column vectors
- M1 for finding a relevant angle e.g. $\tan\theta = (\pm\frac{3}{1})$ or $(\pm\frac{1}{3})$ oe
- First A1 for a correct relevant angle to nearest degree or better
- Second A1 $162°$ (nearest degree is specified)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the value of $p$ and the value of $q$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $(p\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})+(3\mathbf{i}-q\mathbf{j})+(q\mathbf{i}+2p\mathbf{j}) = 2(\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j})$
M1: $p+q+3=2$
M1: $2p-q+2=-6$
A1: $p=-3$
A1: $q=2$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- First M1 for use of F = ma ; M0 if term missing or '2' missing or a = 0
- Second M1, independent but must have sum of at least two force = (m)a, for equating the i cpts, to produce a correct unsimplified equation in p and q only, for their vector equation. M0 if using a = 0
- Third M1, independent but must have at least two forces, for equating the j cpts to produce a correct unsimplified equation in p and q only, for their vector equation. M0 if using a = 0

questions.stem:
Figure 1

A girder $PQ$ has length 4 m and mass 60 kg. A load of mass 30 kg is placed on the girder at $Q$. The loaded girder is held in equilibrium in a horizontal position by two vertical ropes. The ropes are attached to the girder at the points $P$ and $R$, where $RQ = x$ metres, as shown in Figure 1. The tension in the rope at $R$ is four times the tension in the rope at $P$. The girder is modelled as a uniform rod, the ropes as light inextensible strings and the load as a particle.

parts.text:
Find
(i) the tension in the rope at $P$,
(ii) the value of $x$.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $T+4T = 60g+30g$
OR M1 A1 A1: $M(P)$, $60g\times2+30g\times4 = 4T(4-x)$
OR $M(Q)$, $4Tx+T\times4 = 60g\times2$
OR $M(R)$, $T(4-x)+30gx = 60g(2-x)$
OR $M(G)$, $T\times2+30g\times2 = 4T(2-x)$
A1: $T = \frac{90g}{5}$ oe, 176 N or 180 N (Tension at P)
A1: $x = \frac{2}{3}$ (0.67 or better)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- N.B. If T and 4T reversed consistently, treat as one error in any MOMENTS equations so could score max: M1A1M1A1A0A0A0
- First M1 for resolving vertically or a moments equation, with all terms, condone sign errors and missing g's. M0 if a length is missing from a moments equation.
- First A1 for a correct equation in one unknown
- Second M1 for a(nother) moments equation, with all terms, condone sign errors and missing g(s)
- Second and third A1's for a correct equation in two unknowns. Consistent omission of g is one error. A1A0 for one error; A0A0 for two or more errors
- Fourth A1 for any of the 3 answers.
- Fifth A1 for 2/3 oe, 0.67 or better. N.B. This mark can be scored if they have consistently omitted g's. (T = 18)

questions.stem: At time $t=0$, a toy rocket is fired vertically upwards from rest from a point $A$ on the ground. The rocket moves with constant acceleration $2.8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. At time $t=5.25\,\mathrm{s}$, the rocket runs out of fuel and then moves vertically upwards under gravity. At time $t=T$ seconds, the rocket reaches its greatest height above $A$. The rocket is modelled as a particle.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $v = 5.25\times2.8 = 14.7$
M1 A1: $0 = 14.7-9.8t$
A1: $T(=5.25+1.5) = 6.75$ or 6.8
Official notes (completeness pass):
- First M1 for a complete method to find the speed or velocity at t = 5.25 using a = 2.8
- First A1 for 14.7 or – 14.7
- Second M1 for a complete method to produce an (unsimplified) equation in one unknown (either their t or T) using their 14.7 and v = 0. Condone sign errors but need all terms
- Second A1 for a correct equation. Allow if using t = T (A0 if they use g = 9.81, but can score final A1)
- Third A1 for T = 6.75 or 6.8 (as g = 9.8 used)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Without doing any further calculations, sketch a velocity-time graph for the motion of the rocket from when it was fired to when it returns to $A$, showing the value of $T$ on the $t$-axis.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: straight line starting at the origin (1st line)
B1ft: another straight line starting at the end of their first line, with opposite gradient, which crosses the t-axis at $6.75$ OR ft on their $T$. Penalise any extra lines including a solid vertical line at the end
Official notes (completeness pass):
- N.B. Graph could be reflected in the t-axis

questions.stem:
Figure 2

A ring $P$ of mass 0.5 kg is attached to one end of a light inextensible string. The ring is threaded on a fixed rough vertical wire. The ring is held in equilibrium with the string taut. The string makes an angle $\alpha$ with the wire, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{4}{3}$, as shown in Figure 2. The coefficient of friction between $P$ and the wire is $\frac{1}{4}$. The ring is modelled as a particle.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Given that $P$ is on the point of sliding up the wire, find the tension in the string.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $T\sin\alpha = R$
M1 A1: $T\cos\alpha = 0.5g+F$
M1: $F = \frac{1}{4}R$
M1: Solving for T
A1: $T = \frac{5g}{4} = 1.25g = 12$ N or 12.3 N
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (Whole question) If F and R are interchanged, can score max: (a) M0A0M0A0M1M1A0 (b) M0A0M0A0
- First M1 for resolving horizontally, with usual rules
- Second M1 for resolving vertically, with usual rules
- Third A1 cao for any of the 4 alternatives

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the magnitude of the smallest tension in the string which will keep the ring in equilibrium, given that the string remains at angle $\alpha$ to the wire.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $T\cos\alpha = 0.5g-F$
M1: $T\sin\alpha = R$ and $F = \frac{1}{4}R$ and solving for T
A1: $T = \frac{5g}{8} = 0.625g = 6.1$ N or 6.13 N
Official notes (completeness pass):
- First M1 for resolving vertically, with usual rules. N.B. M0 if using the value of R or F and/or T found in part (a)
- Second M1 for the other two equations, which must be correct, and solving for T. N.B. M0 if using the value of R or F and/or T found in part (a)
- Second A1 cao for any of the 4 alternatives
- If the working for (b) is the same as for (a), they can score max M1A0M1A0

questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are horizontal unit vectors due east and due north respectively and position vectors are given relative to a fixed origin $O$.]

Two ships, $P$ and $Q$, are moving with constant velocities. The velocity of $P$ is $(3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$ and the velocity of $Q$ is $(5\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$.

At 9 am, the position vector of $P$ is $(\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})$ km and the position vector of $Q$ is $(7\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j})$ km.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) (i) Write down the position vector of $P$ at time $t$ hours after 9 am.
(ii) Write down the position vector of $Q$ at time $t$ hours after 9 am.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: (i) $\mathbf{r}_P = (\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})+t(3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})$
A1: (ii) $\mathbf{r}_Q = (7\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j})+t(5\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (Whole question) Allow column vectors throughout apart from the given answer in (b)
- M1 for attempt at either or $\mathbf{r}_Q$ with the correct structure oe
- First A1 for a correct expression for $\mathbf{r}_P$ in any form
- Second A1 for a correct expression for $\mathbf{r}_Q$ in any form

parts.label: b
parts.text:
At time $t$ hours after 9 am, $\overrightarrow{QP} = \mathbf{r}$ km.
(b) Show that $\mathbf{r} = (-6-2t)\mathbf{i}+(-4-8t)\mathbf{j}$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\overrightarrow{QP} = (\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})+t(3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})-[(7\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j})+t(5\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})]$
A1: $=(-6-2t)\mathbf{i}+(-4-8t)\mathbf{j}$ Given Answer
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for their $\mathbf{r}_P$ − their $\mathbf{r}_Q$ in any form
- A1 for given answer Must be in i – j form

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Hence find the distance between the ships when $P$ is south west of $Q$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $(-6-2t) = (-4-8t)$
A1: $t=\frac{1}{3}$
M1: $\overrightarrow{QP} = (-6-\frac{2}{3})\mathbf{i}+(-4-\frac{8}{3})\mathbf{j}$
M1: $QP = \sqrt{(-\frac{20}{3})^2+(-\frac{20}{3})^2}$
A1: $=\frac{20\sqrt{2}}{3} = 9.4$ km (or better)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- First M1 for using SW to produce an equation in t only. M0 if they use the ratio i cpt: j cpt = -1
- First A1 for t = 1/3 cao
- Second M1 for substituting their t into QP but can only be scored if t has come from using ratio i cpt: j cpt = 1 or -1. N.B. M0 if t is negative or if they have more than one value of t.
- Third M1 for finding the magnitude of their QP (even if t < 0), but must have found a value for t and substituted it in to give a QP with numerical cpts.
- Second A1 for surd answer, in any form, or 9.4 (km) or better

questions.stem: A car is moving with constant speed along a straight horizontal road. Whenever the brakes are applied they produce a deceleration of $5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. The driver sees a STOP sign which is at the point $S$ on the road ahead. Unfortunately due to the time he takes to react, he does not apply the brakes immediately and the car overshoots the sign. Had he applied the brakes 0.5 s sooner the car would have come to rest at $S$. The car is modelled as a particle.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that, at the instant the car passes $S$, the speed of the car is $2.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $0 = u-0.5\times5$
A1: $u=2.5$ (m s$^{-1}$) Given answer
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for a complete method to obtain an equation in u only and must see v = 0 and a = -5 used. N.B. M0A0 for 5 x 0.5 = 2.5
- A1 for 2.5 (ms$^{-1}$) correctly obtained

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find how far the car travels past $S$ before coming to rest.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $0=2.5^2-2\times5s$
A1: $s=0.625$ (m) oe
OR: $s=\frac{(0+2.5)}{2}\times0.5=0.625$ (m)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for a complete method to obtain an equation in s only

parts.label: c
parts.text:
At the instant when the driver sees the sign, the speed of the car is $64.8\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$. The total time from the instant when the driver first sees the sign to the instant when the car comes to rest is 4.2 seconds.
(c) Find the total distance travelled by the car, from the instant when the driver first sees the sign to the instant when the car reaches the sign.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $64.8$ km h$^{-1}=18$ m s$^{-1}$
M1: $0=18-5t$ OR $2.5=18-5t$
A1ft: $t=3.6$ (on their 18) OR $t=3.1$
M1: any of: $18\times(4.2-t)$ OR $18\times(4.2-0.5-t)$, $s=\frac{1}{2}(18+2.5)\times3.1$, $s=(18\times3.1+\frac{1}{2}\times-5\times3.1^2)$, $s=(2.5\times3.1-\frac{1}{2}\times-5\times3.1^2)$, $2.5^2=18^2+2\times(-5)s$
A1ft: $10.8$ (ft on t & 18)
A1 cao: $31.775$ m
A1 cao: Total distance $=(10.8+31.775)=42.575$ (m)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for 18 (ms$^{-1}$). N.B. If no attempt to change units, only M marks available
- First M1 for finding the time t to decelerate from their 18 to rest OR from 18 to S
- First A1 ft on their 18 and one of their t values found
- Second M1 for an attempt at finding EITHER the distance travelled at their constant speed using a calculated value of OR the distance travelled while decelerating until car passes S
- Second A1 ft for distance travelled at constant speed, ft on their 18 and t value
- Third A1 cao 31.775 (m) (can be unsimplified)
- Fourth A1 for 42.575 (m) cao
